models.h1: Cloudflare Clef API — Multimodal Decisions on KeyoAPI
models.title: Cloudflare Clef API Guide & Pricing | KeyoAPI
models.metaDescription: Cloudflare Clef: open-source 27B multimodal decisions via POST /v1/decisions. Typed choice/noul probabilities, input from $0.063/M, output $0.
models.body:
Cloudflare Clef is an open-source 27B multimodal decision model fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B. The current KeyoAPI endpoint accepts text or image state with typed questions, and returns choice / noul probabilities in a single forward pass without generating free-form text. Use it for request routing, ticket triage and classification.

Call POST /v1/decisions with model cloudflare/clef and a Bearer API key. Check Model Square for current availability and pricing.

guideSections.heading: Context and image limits
paragraphs: The model context is 65536 tokens, but the text state limit on the serving path is much smaller: only approximately the first 2000 text state tokens are read. The remaining text is truncated and not read. Put decision-critical facts first; do not assume a 65536-token state will be processed. Images count separately from this text limit.
Attach at most 4 images as base64 data URLs in PNG, JPEG or WebP format. Remote image URLs are not supported. Each image must be below 300KiB on the current endpoint.

guideSections.heading: Answers and usage
paragraphs: The request contains model, state and questions. Each named question declares a supported type (choice or noul) and its instructions. For a choice question, criteria declares the candidate labels. The response contains answers and usage with input_tokens, output_tokens: 0 and cost. These are structured decision probabilities, not a generated chat message. The current KeyoAPI endpoint does not accept score questions or JSON-object state; send state as supported text or image content.

guideSections.heading: Pricing
paragraphs: Input starts at $0.063 per 1M tokens and output is $0. Each request is billed for its actual usage, and the response’s usage.cost is the final charge in USD. Confirm current prices in Model Square before production traffic.

guideSections.heading: A decision model alongside a chat agent
paragraphs: Use Clef for a defined choice such as account, billing or technical support routing. Your application supplies the candidate labels and decides how to handle low confidence. The returned probabilities are not a guarantee of correctness; evaluate labeled examples and choose thresholds that match the cost of mistakes.

Clef is a Cloudflare decision model, separate from Claude-class chat. See /ai-agent-api for the application execution loop, /claude-api-pricing for chat-model rates and /claude-code-api-pricing for a stated coding-task token budget.

guideSections.heading: Read the final charge from usage.cost
paragraphs: The response usage.cost is the final KeyoAPI charge in USD — use it as returned; no further conversion is needed. Wallet deductions follow the service’s quota precision; output_tokens is 0 for this decision protocol.

At the starting input rate, 1,000 input tokens would estimate $0.000063. This is arithmetic at the starting rate, not a guaranteed request price or a live inference measurement. Use the returned usage.cost and your console usage records for the actual charge.
paragraphsAfter: This is an illustrative usage fragment, not a captured response; the real response also includes id and answers.

faqs.q: Does Clef generate chat or free-form text?
faqs.a: No. A single forward pass returns typed choice / noul probabilities in answers. The current endpoint does not accept score questions. Use POST /v1/decisions.

faqs.q: Can Clef read a 65536-token text state?
faqs.a: Do not rely on it. 65536 is the model context length; the serving text state is truncated after approximately the first 2000 tokens and the remainder is not read. Images count separately.

faqs.q: Can I send remote image URLs?
faqs.a: No. Use up to 4 base64 data URL images in PNG, JPEG or WebP format, each below 300KiB.
No. It is the starting rate. Output is $0, and usage.cost returns the final request charge. Use the returned usage.cost as the actual charge; no further conversion is needed.
No. cloudflare/clef is a Cloudflare decision model. Use /v1/decisions for typed probabilities; use a chat model for free-form explanations or generation.

codeBlocks.title: cURL (Streaming Chat Completion)
Python (openai>=1.0 SDK)
codeBlocks.code:
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ.get("KEYO_API_KEY", "YOUR_API_KEY"),
    base_url="https://www.keyoapi.xyz/v1",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a code analysis agent."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Analyze repository architecture and identify bottlenecks."},
    ],
    temperature=0.6,
    max_tokens=1500,
    stream=True,
)

for chunk in response:
    content = chunk.choices[0].delta.content or ""
    print(content, end="", flush=True)

paragraphs: The metrics above reflect real gateway telemetry measured on 2026-10-19 via automated streaming probes against https://www.keyoapi.xyz/v1/chat/completions using model kimi-k3. Rather than relying on synthetic vendor marketing figures, KeyoAPI captures real-world network and inference behavior directly from active relay channels.

Key observations from our live sampling: Time to First Token (TTFT) has a median of 9,779 ms (p50) and a 95th percentile of 19,962 ms (p95). Because Kimi K3 engages in thorough internal reasoning and context ingestion across its 256K window before emitting its first chunk, interactive applications should always enable streaming mode and display an active generation state to prevent user drop-off.

Under heavy concurrent upstream load, our 15-request sampling recorded 9 successful completions (60.0% uptime) with 6 upstream timeouts or empty response chunks (40.0% error rate). In production architectures, client applications must implement exponential backoff retries (minimum 2s initial delay) or configure automatic fallback routing to deepseek-v4.1-flash or glm-5.3 for latency-critical paths.

paragraphs: KeyoAPI provides unified billing and a consistent OpenAI-compatible endpoint across all major model families. The table below compares kimi-k3 with top alternative reasoning and chat models available in our catalog to help engineering teams choose the right tier for each stage of their pipelines.
rows: Ultra-long context document analysis, deep reasoning & autonomous coding agents
High-throughput classification, agent intent routing & fast summarization
Complex multi-step system design, legal contract review & nuanced literature
General chat, structured data extraction & balanced enterprise reasoning
paragraphsAfter: Notice that kimi-k3 provides 256K tokens of context—larger than Claude Sonnet 5 (200K) or GPT-5.6 Luna (128K)—while costing only ~$0.20 / $1.02 per million tokens. This represents a 93% cost reduction compared to proprietary Western frontier models, making large-context agent loops economically viable at enterprise volume.

guideSections.heading: Production Workload Cost Simulation (1,000 Support Conversations)
paragraphs: To ground token prices in actual budgeting numbers, consider an automated tier-2 customer support workload consisting of 1,000 multi-turn customer conversations.

In a typical enterprise support session, the conversation history, retrieved internal documentation, and ticket context consume approximately 1,800 input tokens. The model's synthesized diagnosis and actionable step-by-step resolution require approximately 400 output tokens.
For a batch of 1,000 conversations, total token consumption equals: 1,000 × 1,800 = 1,800,000 input tokens (1.8M), and 1,000 × 400 = 400,000 output tokens (0.4M).

Applying KeyoAPI’s kimi-k3 sell rates: Input cost = 1.8M × $0.20 / 1M = $0.360. Output cost = 0.4M × $1.02 / 1M = $0.408. Total cost for 1,000 resolved tickets = $0.360 + $0.408 = $0.768 (approximately $0.77 total).

At less than $0.00077 per customer interaction, developers can run comprehensive multi-agent retrieval and verification steps on every ticket without inflating operational burn rates. Running this same batch through claude-sonnet-5 ($3.00 / $15.00) would cost $11.40—over 14 times more expensive.

faqs.q: How do I call kimi-k3 on KeyoAPI?
faqs.a: Point any standard OpenAI SDK or HTTP client base URL to https://www.keyoapi.xyz/v1, set Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY, and provide model=kimi-k3 in your POST /v1/chat/completions payload. No specialized SDK or adapter is required.

faqs.q: Is there a free path for Kimi K3 API key prototyping?
faqs.a: Yes. Every new account registered at /sign-up receives a one-time $10 welcome balance. For risk-free testing without drawing down paid credits, use gift-credit model IDs on /free-models. Once your schemas and logic are verified, switch model= to kimi-k3 on the exact same API key and base URL.

faqs.q: What context window does kimi-k3 support?
faqs.a: kimi-k3 features an ultra-large 256K token context window (approximately 200,000 English words or 400,000 Chinese characters). This enables feeding entire code repositories, financial filings, and long conversational histories directly in prompt context.

faqs.q: Is the model ID kimi-k3 case-sensitive?
faqs.a: Yes. The exact API model string must be kimi-k3 in lowercase. Calling Kimi-K3, KIMI-K3, or moonshot-k3 will fail validation and return a model_not_found error from the gateway.

faqs.q: Who is the upstream vendor behind Kimi K3?
faqs.a: Kimi K3 is developed by Moonshot AI (北京月之暗面科技有限公司), a prominent frontier AI lab specializing in ultra-long context reasoning architectures, complex mathematical deduction, and agentic reinforcement learning.

faqs.q: Does kimi-k3 support streaming and function calling?
faqs.a: Yes. Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming via stream=true is fully supported for real-time token delivery. OpenAI-compatible tools and function calling parameters are also recognized for building agent workflows.

faqs.q: How does kimi-k3 compare to deepseek-v4.1-flash for agent loops?
faqs.a: deepseek-v4.1-flash is a lower-cost model (~$0.14 / $0.56 per 1M) with a 128K context window, best optimized for rapid intent classification and message triage. kimi-k3 (~$0.20 / $1.02 per 1M) offers twice the context window (256K) and superior SWE-bench verified coding capabilities (79.0%), making it the superior choice for primary code execution and long-document reasoning.

faqs.q: What error codes should I handle and what is the recommended retry policy?
faqs.a: Monitor for HTTP 429 (rate limits) and HTTP 504 / 502 (upstream vendor timeout during peak traffic). Implement exponential backoff with jitter (starting at 2s). For mission-critical endpoints requiring strict sub-5s response guarantees, configure client-side fallback to deepseek-v4.1-flash or glm-5.3 on the same Keyo key.

guideSections.heading: GPT 6.1 Sol pricing and a request-cost example
paragraphs: The public KeyoAPI catalog checked on 2026-10-13 lists default-group rates of $0.3677 per million input tokens and $1.8385 per million output tokens. These are KeyoAPI sell rates, not official OpenAI list prices. Other billing groups can apply a multiplier; confirm your active group and current rates on /pricing.

For 10,000 input tokens and 2,000 output tokens, the ordinary token estimate is 0.01 × $0.3677 + 0.002 × $1.8385 = $0.007354. A thousand requests with that identical mix total about $7.354 before retries, cached-token adjustments or extra modalities. Use actual response usage when calculating a production budget.

guideSections.heading: GPT-6.1 Sol vs GPT-6 Astra
paragraphs: Astra lists $1.8385 input and $9.1925 output per million tokens in the checked default group. Sol therefore costs one fifth as much per input or output token. The same 10,000-input and 2,000-output example costs $0.036770 on Astra. The complete table and evaluation checklist are on /gpt-6-1-sol-vs-gpt-6-astra.

Choose using accepted task results, not the model names alone. Compare identical prompts, correctness, latency, output lengths and retries. Start a Sol evaluation on routine chat or structured work, then test Astra on cases that fail your acceptance checks. Higher unit prices do not by themselves prove better coding or reasoning quality.

guideSections.heading: Use the exact Sol model ID
paragraphs: GPT Sol 6.1 and GPT 6.1 Sol refer to gpt-6.1-sol in this catalog. Pass that exact ID to POST /v1/chat/completions; the words in a search phrase are not interchangeable API aliases. Check optional tool, streaming and context behavior on the channel you use before depending on those features.

For an application workflow see /ai-agent-api, /ai-story-api or /study-ai-api. For a broader GPT-class token table see /openai-api-pricing. These examples use the bare paid model ID; gift-credit eligibility is tied to eligible gift-credit IDs rather than automatically applied to every chat model.
